questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Sydney because it was an english speaking country far away from Denmark where you don't just get to live another time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: University of Sydney was very informative with a lot of emails from the exchange coordinator beforehand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a welcome day exclusive to exchange students where we were told relevant information about everything from studying to life in Sydney.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You were guaranteed a student accommodation however this was not all on campus. I lived at The Queen Mary Building

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was no meal plan but a big kitchen where you could cook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Do it! It was not the greatest facilities but it was a really good place to meet people and the community was so nice. You have to apply quickly when you get the email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to fill out personal information of different sort but the guiding was very good so it was not a problem.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guides with pictures and you could write the exchange coordinator if you had any doubts.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses i wanted - it was not a problem for any chemistry courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get it done quickly so you don't miss out on housing offers.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two level 3000 courses which is 3rd year courses, but in Australia they often have minors, so the courses were a bit lower level than at home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We didn't have any "regnetimer" where you sat with a teacher. We only had lectures and laboratory.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Programming
Learning in Outdoor Education
Molecular Self-Assembly
Computational Chemistry

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Learning in Outdoor Education was an amazing course to lake off some workload while at the same time meeting a lot of people from all over the world and learning about the Australian nature.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Cleaning fees at the student accommodation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol was more expensive to buy in stores, but cheaper in bars.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many societies across campus which you are introduced too in the welcome week during what they call "Welcome Fest".

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was a part of the yoga society which was very nice! Also the student union offered a lot of free day trips which are worth a try.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as possible but also enjoy your weekends getting to know Sydney. Go to Tasmania! We did it in the spring break and it was amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adjust. Compared to it being the other side of the world it felt very european.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
It was hard to socialise with local students because they often just want to get home after class and the student accommodation
is mostly exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was not challenging - they are very friendly and always want to help you.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a bit of aboriginal culture and how complex it is. Barbecues on the beach (and everywhere else) is a big thing with free places to do it, which you should definitely do!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Spend a lot of time socialising in the beginning! This is when you build friendships and friend groups. 
Live at a student accommodation- it makes it so much easier to meet and socialise with people.
Use the student union, USU - they offer so many things including free food on a weekly basis.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy - time flies by!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many nice people from all around the world. It really broadens your perspective a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time difference between Australia and Denmark. It is a bit hard to coordinate phone calls with people at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
